output.summary: Three causes confound: the Corvane steel switch (3 Aug), spindle degradation (runout and vibration rising), and the 12-hour shifts. The Corvane high-spread lots ran later (weeks 37-41), so lot spread is confounded with time and wear. New operators rejected at the same rate as experienced ones, and FPY had already fallen by week 34, so that hypothesis is contradicted. Rejects look real (handling rejects steady). The best action is a staggered, controlled A2 trial that separates service status from bar source and recovers hour of machining. Reverting shifts or steel now, punishing operators, or cutting CMM inspection are unjustified or harmful. Q2 (Line 6 CMM) separates steel from spindle wear. Q3 tests fatigue.
